title: Ten minutes that made a lifesaving difference
summary: How ADT Monitoring helped a Texas family escape a fast-moving fire and save what mattered most.
body_markdown:
ADT customer Karla Rodriguez holds a baby photo she was able to rescue before a fire at a neighbor's house reached her own. She was alerted to the fire at the neighbor's by her own ADT smoke detector.


Just before 4:30 a.m. on March 25, 2026, Karla Rodriguez* awoke to chaos. Her mother had woken her after hearing unusual crackling sounds and discovering that their neighbor's home was on fire. As smoke spread into the family’s home, their ADT-monitored alarm sounded, cutting through the confusion.


Moments later, ADT Monitoring Agent Kenisha Liptrot called to verify the alarm. Rodriguez explained that there was a fire, it was spreading fast and they couldn’t find their dog, Rocco.


As the family scrambled to exit before the fire reached their home, Liptrot contacted the fire department. Those few extra minutes helped prevent a catastrophe, Rodriguez said.


“It’s very important to have life safety systems like this in your home because they can definitely save your life,” she said. “Whether it be five minutes or 10 minutes, those minutes are very crucial because they not only saved us and our dog, Rocco, but most of the belongings inside our home.”


### A steady voice on the line


ADT Monitoring Agent Kenisha Liptrot


Liptrot knew the situation was serious as soon as she heard Rodriguez’s frantic voice on the other end of the line.


“The best thing to do is put yourself in the customer’s shoes,” Liptrot said. “Maintaining a calm, soothing voice keeps them at ease and lets them know they are going to receive the assistance they need in a timely manner.”


After verifying the alarm, Liptrot connected with the fire department and shared critical information about the family’s dog. That information helped firefighters begin looking for Rocco as soon as they arrived and bring him to safety.


“Our job isn’t just a job. It actually makes a difference in someone’s life,” Liptrot said.


### Early detection and a coordinated response


Firefighters arrived before the flames had fully spread to the Rodriguez home, allowing them to attack the fire and protect areas that had not yet been affected.


“Fire and smoke don’t have any mercy,” said Pasadena Fire Chief David Brannon. “You need that early detection to be able to escape a structure.”


Professionally monitored systems enhance the protection offered by a smoke detector alone.[ADT’s trained monitoring professionals](https://newsroom.adt.com/employee-experience/what-makes-adt-monitoring-different-5-reasons-it-stands-out) are available around the clock to help verify alarm events and contact emergency assistance when every second matters.


“We’re the eyes and ears,” Liptrot said. “You have someone who’s there for you, who’s looking out for you.”


### Meeting the voice behind the call


Months after the fire, the family met Liptrot in person, the calm voice who had supported them on the phone that morning. During the reunion, Liptrot received ADT’s Life Saver Award in recognition of her outstanding customer care.


As Rodriguez and Liptrot embraced, they reflected on an event that could have ended very differently.


“Before the fire, we always thought of our ADT system as a surveillance camera to make sure things were not stolen,” Rodriguez said. “We really didn’t think about it saving lives until the fire happened.”


Rodriguez said the early warning gave her family critical time to respond to the threat.


“I want to emphasize those 10 extra minutes with the fire alarm,” she said. “We were able to get out safely, and I think it prevented even greater damage to our home.”


ADT’s life safety devices can detect smoke, carbon monoxide, and heat. With 24/7 ADT Monitoring, early detection can save seconds, when every second counts. For more information, visit[adt.com/life-safety](https://www.adt.com/life-safety) .
